title: Grove Artifact edits pass on a simple majority of votes cast, with abstentions excluded and no quorum requirement
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 sets the voting rule in one sentence: "The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved." Token holders "may vote directly or through Delegates."

The notable absence is a **quorum**. The threshold is relative to votes cast, not to supply, so approval depends only on the ratio among those who show up. With low participation, a small coordinated holding can pass an edit to the Artifact. This is a deliberate trade: it prevents governance deadlock from apathy, at the cost of making outcomes sensitive to turnout.

Excluding abstentions sharpens the same effect — abstaining does not raise the bar for approval, it removes the abstainer from the denominator entirely. Abstention is therefore not a soft "no"; it is complete withdrawal.

The governance calendar adds a second, subtler discretion. Grove "runs in a weekly cycle that begins every Monday," with a submission cut-off of "Wednesday 16:00 UTC"; after the cut-off, "it is at the discretion of the Operational Facilitator whether the proposal can be included in the immediate next cycle, or the following cycle." The section then states that proposals not requiring Core Council Risk Advisor approval "may instead follow the later end-of-Friday submission deadline" — so the effective deadline depends on the Facilitator's own risk classification made in the prior step.
description: A three-day Snapshot poll needs only more than 50% of non-abstaining votes in favour, so a cleared proposal can carry on very low turnout; voting may be direct or delegated.
